title: Quantum Geometric Origin of Yu-Shiba-Rusinov States
abstract: In this work, we revisit the classic Yu-Shiba-Rusinov (YSR) problem of magnetic impurities in $s$-wave superconductors and uncover a quantum geometric origin of the YSR bound-state structure. The key geometric quantity is the momentum-space average of Bloch band projector over low-energy electrons, whose matrix rank, positive eigenvalues, and corresponding eigenvectors directly control the number, energies, and symmetry representations of the YSR states, respectively. As a result, a superconductor with nontrivial normal-state quantum geometry can host more bound states than its trivial counterpart, even if they share the same electronic dispersion. We apply our theory to monolayer $1H$-NbSe$_2$ and find that the geometric texture of its single superconducting band enforces three symmetry-distinct YSR channels for a magnetic point impurity at Nb or Se sites. Our work opens a route to probing normal-state wavefunction geometry through local YSR spectroscopy.
summary: This paper establishes that the physics of Yu-Shiba-Rusinov bound states in superconductors is fundamentally governed by the quantum geometry of the normal-state electronic bands. By analyzing the band projector, the authors predict the number and energy of these states, demonstrating that the geometry dictates the superconducting response, which is tested successfully on monolayer NbSe2.
main_problem: To uncover the quantum geometric origin governing the Yu-Shiba-Rusinov (YSR) bound-state structure induced by magnetic impurities in s-wave superconductors.
main_result: The number and energies of YSR states are dictated by the rank and eigenvalues of the Brillouin-zone averaged band projector ($Q$ or $Q_{FS}$), revealing a deep connection between normal-state quantum geometry and superconducting properties.
method: The theory utilizes the T-matrix formalism and analyzes the eigensystem of the quantum geometric projector ($Q$), which is derived from the normal-state Green's function in the flat-band or weak-pairing limit.
model_or_system: The study models magnetic impurities in conventional s-wave superconductors, applying the theory to the monolayer 1H-NbSe2 using a multi-orbital tight-binding framework.
key_observables: The number of YSR states ($N_{YSR} = 	ext{rank } Q$), the YSR bound-state energies ($E_{	ext{YSR}}$), and the symmetry representations of the bound states.
important_parameters: The geometric projector $Q$, the exchange coupling strength $J$, and the Fermi level ($\mu=0$ or $\mu$ scanning).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the flat-band limit for initial derivation and the weak-pairing limit for the application to dispersive bands. It assumes time-reversal invariance and s-wave pairing.

paper_structure: The paper first establishes the general theory by defining the geometric quantity $Q$ and relating its rank to $N_{YSR}$. It then applies this framework to simplified models (flat-band limit) before extending the theory to realistic materials like monolayer 1H-NbSe2, comparing predictions with full T-matrix calculations.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, general theoretical tool—linking topological/geometric invariants of the normal state to observable spectroscopic features in the superconducting state—which is highly relevant for understanding emergent phenomena in strongly correlated superconducting materials.
